debug group help:
  list, io, alwaysflush, skipstackwalk, timestamp, exit, beep, clear, add, view, windowed, fulldump, errors

list (g|l|d|a|c) [ <pattern> ]

Shows some or all items of a specific type.

The following items are supported:
- g: command groups
- l: log groups (only those encountered yet)
- d: log groups with descriptions (only those that have descriptions)
- a: asserts (only those hit yet)
- c: crashes (only

alwaysflush [ (+|-) ]

Enables/disables flushing after each new entry in
the log file (default: off).

skipstackwalk [ (+|-) ]

Enables/disables stack walk feature
the log file (default: off).

timestamp [ (+|-) ]

Enables/disables timestamping each log entry
(default: off).

beep

Causes a beep on the internal system speaker.

clear (l|a|c)

Clears the given inclusion/exclusion list
(l=logs, a=asserts, c=crashes).

add (l|a|c) (+|-) <pattern>

Adds a pattern to the given list (l=logs, 
a=asserts, c=crashes). By default all
asserts and crashes are active, all logs
inactive. Each item is then checked 
against all pattern in the respective
list. If a match is found the active/inactive
state is modified accordingl

view [ (l|a|c) ]

Shows the active pattern for the given list
(l=logs, a=asserts, c=crashes).

windowed [ (+|-) ]

Enables/disables windowed mode thus overriding any
auto-detected status.

fulldump [ (+|-) ]

Enables/disables full memory dumps on crash (default: off).

errors [ (+|-) ]

Enables/disables extra logging of DERRORs into errors.txt (default: on).

flat I/O help:
The following I/O commands are defined:
  add, copy, splitadd, splitview, splitremove
Type in debug.io flat help <cmd> for a detailed command help.

add [ <filename> [ <size in kb> ] ]

Create flat file I/O (optionally specifying file name and file size).
If a filename is specified all output is written to that file. Otherwise
the magic filename '*eMN' is automatically used. Any existing files with
that name are overwritten.

Instead of a real f

copy <directory>

Copies generated log file(s) into the given directory if the program
exists or crashes. If there is already a log file with the same
name a unique number is appended to the current log files' name.

splitadd <types> <filter> <name> [ <size in kb> ]

Splits off part of the log data. Multiple splits can be defined. They 
are written out to the first matching split file.

'types' defines one or more string types which should be split off:
- a: asserts
- c: crash
- l: logs
- x: exceptions
- r: repl

splitview

Shows all existing splits in the order they are evaluated.

splitremove <namepattern>

Removes all active splits matching the given name pattern.
